points.description: First correct objective stated precisely with the correct term from the model answer (e.g. support for billions of end-systems / larger address space; reduce routing tables; simplified header; increased security; real-time/QoS support via flow label and traffic class; multicasting; mobility/roaming; extensibility via extension headers; coexistence with existing protocols).
points.partial_credit: Objective is named but only vaguely (e.g. 'better performance') — no part marks; award half only if the idea is clearly right but lacks the key term.

points.description: Second distinct correct objective from the model answer list, stated precisely with the correct term.
points.partial_credit: Idea clearly right but key term missing: half.

points.description: Third distinct correct objective from the model answer list, stated precisely with the correct term.
points.partial_credit: Idea clearly right but key term missing: half.

points.description: Fourth distinct correct objective from the model answer list, stated precisely with the correct term.
points.partial_credit: Idea clearly right but key term missing: half.

rubric.notes: Full marks need at least four distinct, correct IPv6 objectives from the model answer list, each worth 0.25. Each objective must be stated precisely with the right term (e.g. simplified header, flow label/QoS, extension headers); vague or generic statements such as 'faster' or 'better' earn nothing. A wrong or non-IPv6 objective earns nothing for that point, and repeated objectives count once.
